review.summary: I wrote 17 tests covering Rust, Swift and Lua and ran them. Four failed, all from one defect: Rust doesn't recognise a character literal that holds a simple escape (`'\n'`, `'\''`, `'\\'`, `'\"'`). In `rustCharEnd` (src/dialects.ts), after a backslash the code does `j += 3`, which looks for the closing `'` one character too far right. Only `\x..` and `\u{..}` escapes work. When a simple escape fails to register, a `"` inside or right after it opens a string. Rust strings can run over lines, so the lines after it are counted as code instead of comments. The diff's own `'\''` and `'\\'` tests pass only because nothing on those lines exposes the mistake. The four failing tests are in test/probe-dialects.test.ts and the 13 passing ones were deleted. Nothing I tested in Swift or Lua failed: nested comments, raw strings with any number of `#`, `""` before a comment, long comments and long strings of any level, escapes, and `---[[`.

findings.test: test/probe-dialects.test.ts > probe Rust > reads '\"' as a character literal, not a string opener (also: reads b'\"' as a byte character literal; reads '\'' as a character literal before another; reads '\n' as a character literal)
findings.text: `rustCharEnd` (src/dialects.ts) skips 3 characters past the backslash for a simple escape (`j += 3` with `j` already at the backslash), so it looks for the closing `'` at at+4 instead of at+3. The goal says `'\n'`, `'\''` and `'\\'` are character literals, but none of them is read as one. Example: `let q = '\"'; // c` followed by `// d` gives code 2, comments 0; the right answer is code 1, comments 1. The `"` inside the literal opens a multi-line Rust string, which swallows the next line. The same happens with `b'\"'` and with `('\'','"')` and `('\n','"')`: the escape literal is missed, so the quotes pair up wrongly and a `"` opens a string.

failed: probe Rust reads '\"' as a character literal, not a string opener
probe Rust reads b'\"' as a byte character literal
probe Rust reads '\'' as a character literal before another
probe Rust reads '\n' as a character literal
